<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this appendix, we verify the generality of the IQL based analyses in Sections <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Gradient Conflicts among Robots ‣ 5 Gradient Conflicts and Resolution via Embodiment-Based Grouping ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> and <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Correlation between Embodiment Distance and the Gradient Conflicts ‣ 5 Gradient Conflicts and Resolution via Embodiment-Based Grouping ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>, which linked gradient conflicts to suboptimality, embodiment diversity, and embodiment similarity, by repeating the same study with another offline RL algorithm, TD3+BC. Concretely, when we apply our gradient conflict analyses to TD3+BC, we find that (i) the fraction of negative pairwise gradient cosine similarities increases as the proportion of suboptimal data grows, (ii) the same fraction also increases as we enlarge the number and morphological diversity of robots, and (iii) these gradient conflicts are strongly structured by embodiment similarity, since robots that are closer in the morphology graph exhibit more aligned policy gradients. Taken together, the IQL and TD3+BC results indicate that the observed relationships between suboptimality, embodiment diversity, embodiment similarity, and gradient conflicts are general properties of cross embodiment offline RL rather than artifacts of a particular actor update.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>Gradient conflicts under TD3+BC.</h3>

<div id="A7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each embodiment <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the TD3+BC actor loss <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}^{\pi,\mathrm{TD3+BC}}_{\tau}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>TD3</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>BC</mi></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}^{\pi,\mathrm{TD3+BC}}_{\tau}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> on the subset of transitions belonging to robot <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, and denote its gradient by <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\tau}=\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}^{\pi,\mathrm{TD3+BC}}_{\tau}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>TD3</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>BC</mi></mrow></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\tau}=\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}^{\pi,\mathrm{TD3+BC}}_{\tau}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>. As in Section <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Gradient Conflicts among Robots ‣ 5 Gradient Conflicts and Resolution via Embodiment-Based Grouping ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>, we measure inter embodiment alignment using pairwise cosine similarities <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C[\tau_{i},\tau_{j}]\;=\;{\langle g_{\tau_{i}},\,g_{\tau_{j}}\rangle}/{\|g_{\tau_{i}}\|\,\|g_{\tau_{j}}\|}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C[\tau_{i},\tau_{j}]\;=\;{\langle g_{\tau_{i}},\,g_{\tau_{j}}\rangle}/{\|g_{\tau_{i}}\|\,\|g_{\tau_{j}}\|}.</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A7.F14.sf1" title="In Appendix G Additional correlation analysis for TD3+BC ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14(a)</span></a> reports, over the course of training, the fraction of negative pairwise cosine similarities (<math id="A7.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C[\tau_{i},\tau_{j}]&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C[\tau_{i},\tau_{j}]&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math>) under the Expert Forward, 30% Suboptimal Replay Forward, and 70% Suboptimal Replay Forward datasets. We observe the same qualitative trend as in the IQL case: as the proportion of suboptimal data increases, the fraction of negative cosines also increases, indicating more frequent gradient conflicts between robots. This confirms that the emergence of strong gradient conflicts in the presence of abundant suboptimal data is not tied to the particular choice of IQL and also occurs for TD3+BC. To further investigate the relationship between positive and negative transfer and gradient conflicts under TD3+BC, we compute the correlation coefficient between each robot’s reward difference (cross-embodiment minus single-robot training) and its average TD3+BC gradient cosine similarity with all other robots in the 70% Suboptimal Replay Forward dataset, using robots with substantial performance changes (absolute reward difference greater than <math id="A7.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>), which are highlighted in Table <a href="#A7.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Appendix G Additional correlation analysis for TD3+BC ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>. The resulting correlation, <math id="A7.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=0.766" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.766</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=0.766</annotation></semantics></math>, indicates a strong positive relationship: robots that exhibit large negative transfer exhibit greater gradient conflict. These findings mirror the IQL results and further support that gradient conflicts underlie the negative transfer observed when applying cross-embodiment learning to datasets rich in suboptimal data.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We also examine how gradient conflicts evolve with embodiment diversity under TD3+BC. Using the 70% Suboptimal Replay Forward dataset, we gradually expand the set of robots included in cross embodiment training, starting from a small, morphologically homogeneous quadruped subset (Unitree A1, Go1, Go2), then all nine quadrupeds, and finally all 16 robots. For each configuration, we compute, for every robot, the fraction of negative pairwise cosine similarities with the other robots and average this quantity across robots. Figure <a href="#A7.F14.sf2" title="In Appendix G Additional correlation analysis for TD3+BC ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14(b)</span></a> shows that, as we add more diverse embodiments, the fraction of negative TD3+BC cosine similarities increases, just as in the IQL case. In other words, greater embodiment diversity leads to more frequent TD3+BC gradient conflicts, making negative transfer more likely when the dataset is rich in suboptimal trajectories.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.2 </span>Correlation with embodiment similarity</h3>

<div id="A7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we analyze how TD3+BC gradient alignment across robots is captured by the same embodiment similarity measure used in Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Correlation between Embodiment Distance and the Gradient Conflicts ‣ 5 Gradient Conflicts and Resolution via Embodiment-Based Grouping ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>. We reuse the FGW based embodiment similarity matrix and construct the corresponding mean TD3+BC gradient cosine similarity matrix by averaging <math id="A7.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C[\tau_{i},\tau_{j}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C[\tau_{i},\tau_{j}]</annotation></semantics></math> over training for each robot pair.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A7.F15.sf1" title="In Figure 15 ‣ G.2 Correlation with embodiment similarity ‣ Appendix G Additional correlation analysis for TD3+BC ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15(a)</span></a> shows the resulting embodiment-based similarity matrix, while Figure <a href="#A7.F15.sf2" title="In Figure 15 ‣ G.2 Correlation with embodiment similarity ‣ Appendix G Additional correlation analysis for TD3+BC ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15(b)</span></a> presents the corresponding matrix of mean TD3+BC gradient cosine similarities. As in the IQL case, morphologically similar quadrupeds form a tight cluster in both matrices. Figure <a href="#A7.F15.sf3" title="In Figure 15 ‣ G.2 Correlation with embodiment similarity ‣ Appendix G Additional correlation analysis for TD3+BC ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15(c)</span></a> further visualizes this relationship as a scatter plot between embodiment similarity and mean TD3+BC gradient cosine similarity. The Pearson correlation coefficient between these two quantities is <math id="A7.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{r=0.711}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>=</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">0.711</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r=0.711}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A7.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=\,8.89\times 10^{-20}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn> 8.89</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=\,8.89\times 10^{-20}</annotation></semantics></math> , indicating a strong positive correlation: robot pairs that are more similar in embodiment tend to have more aligned TD3+BC policy gradients. Together with the IQL results in Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Correlation between Embodiment Distance and the Gradient Conflicts ‣ 5 Gradient Conflicts and Resolution via Embodiment-Based Grouping ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>, this supports the validity of embodiment based grouping as a general, morphology driven mechanism for reducing gradient conflicts in cross embodiment offline RL.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.F15" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="A7.F15.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18025v1/images/etas_fixed.png" id="A7.F15.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:548/533;" width="548" height="533" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(a) </span>Embodiment-based similarity matrix</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="A7.F15.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18025v1/images/grad_matrix_td3.png" id="A7.F15.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:548/519;" width="548" height="519" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(b) </span>Average gradient cosine similarity matrix (TD3+BC)</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="A7.F15.sf3" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18025v1/images/Robsymgrad_td3.png" id="A7.F15.sf3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:548/547;" width="548" height="547" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(c) </span>Embodiment-based similarity vs. mean gradient cosine similarity (TD3+BC)</figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 15: </span>(a) Embodiment-based similarity matrix (1 <math id="A7.F15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> min-max-normalized FGW distance between robot pairs);
(b) Average gradient cosine similarity matrix for TD3+BC on the Expert Forward dataset, with the color scale compressed for readability using a symlog normalization;
(c) Scatter plot of embodiment-based similarity and mean gradient cosine similarity for all robot pairs under TD3+BC.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Applying Embodiment Grouping to the Critic</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Algorithm <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Embodiment-Grouped Offline RL Update ‣ 5 Gradient Conflicts and Resolution via Embodiment-Based Grouping ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a> applies Embodiment Grouping (EG) to the actor updates, while the critic is updated once per outer iteration using the global minibatch. This design is motivated by our analysis that negative transfer in heterogeneous cross-embodiment offline RL is mainly caused by policy-gradient conflict. Here we examine whether extending EG to critic learning further improves performance.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setup.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate a variant, denoted as EG-Actor+Critic, that applies EG to the critic in addition to the actor. Specifically, after sampling a global minibatch <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, we split it into group-specific minibatches <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{B_{m}\}_{m=1}^{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{B_{m}\}_{m=1}^{M}</annotation></semantics></math> using the same embodiment clusters as the actor update. We then update the critic sequentially over each <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., performing <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> critic updates per outer iteration), followed by the standard EG actor updates. All other training configurations follow Section <a href="#S6" title="6 Experimental Evaluation ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Results.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A8.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ Results. ‣ Appendix H Applying Embodiment Grouping to the Critic ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> reports results on the <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">70% Suboptimal Replay Forward</span> dataset. Applying EG to the critic yields no meaningful improvement over actor-only EG, and slightly degrades performance for <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=4</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.T10" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span>Ablation on applying Embodiment Grouping to the critic. <table id="A8.T10.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A8.T10.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.T10.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt">Group count <math id="A8.T10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math></th>

</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Discussion.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although extending EG to the critic is conceptually possible, the results in Table <a href="#A8.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ Results. ‣ Appendix H Applying Embodiment Grouping to the Critic ‣ Cross-Embodiment Offline Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Robot Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> show that it does not bring additional return gains over the actor-only variant in our setting. Moreover, this extension comes with a clear practical drawback: the critic must be optimized separately within each group, leading to a substantial increase in wall-clock training time. EG is mainly introduced to mitigate policy-gradient conflicts, and actor-only EG already provides strong performance improvements. Given the limited benefit and the extra cost of critic-side grouping, we apply EG only to the actor in the main method.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Hyperparameters and Training Details</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix summarizes the hyperparameters and training procedures used for reproducibility.
Unless otherwise noted, values are shared across all robots.</p>
</div>

<tr id="A9.T12.2.7" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A9.T12.2.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row">Discount factor <math id="A9.T12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math></th>
<td id="A9.T12.2.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">0.99</td></tr>
<tr id="A9.T12.2.8" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A9.T12.2.8.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row">GAE <math id="A9.T12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math></th>
<td id="A9.T12.2.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">0.9</td></tr>
<tr id="A9.T12.2.9" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A9.T12.2.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row">Clip range (PPO <math id="A9.T12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>)</th>
<td id="A9.T12.2.9.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">0.1</td></tr>
<tr id="A9.T12.2.10" class="ltx_tr">
